newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian avg lending rate falls to 7.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian avg lending rate falls to 7.8 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate, weighed down by call money loans, fell to 7.8 percent on Monday from 8.6 percent.
Trade volume rose to 84.8 million kuna from Friday's 53.5 million on the back of stronger interbank demand ahead of the reserve payment. Of this 73 million were fresh deals, mostly call money.
The interbank call money rate was steady at 7.0 percent, with term rates ranging between the eight-day 8.5 percent and 13 percent for 60-day kuna.
Savings banks paid 15 percent for 14-day kuna due to their perceived higher repayment risk.
Insurers rolled over call money loans at six percent and one-month loans at 9.0 and 13 percent.
The kuna mid-rate eased to 6.6568 versus 6.5760 to the dollar previously, while firming very slightly to 3.5610 against the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
